# Halo

> Halo is an open-source (MIT) desktop AI workstation for macOS, Windows and Linux. Day to day it works like a desktop AI workbench (chat, code, documents, research) with pluggable agent engines: Claude Code, Codex, Halo SDK and DeepSeek dsh. Beyond that, it runs Digital Humans — AI members that stay on duty on schedules or events — and puts them in teams that divide work, hand it over and deliver results, including with colleagues' Digital Humans on their own computers. Work can be handed off from a phone, Feishu, WeChat or WeCom.

Key facts:
- Open source, free; runs on the user's own computer; Halo has no backend service of its own.
- Sign in with Claude, ChatGPT or GitHub Copilot accounts, or use any Anthropic / OpenAI-compatible API.
- Digital Human teams are decentralized: no central server; team state follows a Raft-inspired design (majority-elected leading node, term-based log replication, automatic re-election).
- Built-in AI browser, AI terminal, knowledge base, Office document skills (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, PDF), MCP and Skills.
- Requirements: macOS 12+ (Apple silicon and Intel), Windows 10+ x64, Linux glibc 2.34+; Android app is a remote client.
- Written almost entirely by Halo itself: over 500,000 lines of code.
